findings.description: Rules section references rules via absolute local filesystem paths that are machine-specific and will break on any other machine or CI environment.
Branch check is inline prose without a labeled '## Step 1 — Branch check' heading, unlike every other command.
Branch check is inline prose without a labeled '## Step 1 — Branch check' heading, unlike every other command.
No branch check step at all; every other write-capable command guards on main/master before doing any work.
No branch check step even though it writes files (.claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md) that should only be committed from main.
Uses free-form section headings instead of the '## Step N — Name' pattern used by all other commands.
Uses 'source': './' with no explicit include/files list; every file added to the repo root is silently bundled into the plugin distribution.
Bootstrap procedure instruction ('Perform this scan during project bootstrap') is mixed with standing operational rules, causing agents to potentially re-execute it on every load.
Mermaid flow diagram shows approval nodes with only |yes| branches; none have a |no|/stop path even though the command halts on decline.
Approval gate in Task 3 is buried mid-list rather than called out as a hard stop, risking agents treating it as optional prose.
Conditional self-advance ('proceed to Step 3 when approved') conflicts with the explicit stop-and-wait gate pattern used in Steps 4 and 5.
Jekyll exclude list manually enumerates directories; every new top-level directory must be manually added or it will be included in the site build.
No branch check step even though it commits in Step 5 Task 6, diverging from every other file-writing command.
Uses free-form section headings ('Assessment', 'Full', 'Gap') instead of '## Step N — Name' pattern.
Uses free-form section headings ('Assessment', 'Full', 'Gap') instead of '## Step N — Name' pattern.
The docs page clarifies 'the file is not procedural' but the shipped rules/safety.md has no equivalent — agents read the rule file, not the doc.
Rules index page is a stub with no child-file links, no summary of what each rule covers, and no guidance on when to use which.
No '## Stop conditions' section; uses '## Approval gates' instead, breaking the structural template every other command page follows.
Scoped verification pass is numbered '8.5' in the doc but '7.5' in the command definition, creating a numbering mismatch.
See also entries use ' - ' (hyphen) as separator; majority of other command docs use ' — ' (em-dash).
See also entries use ' - ' (hyphen) as separator; majority of other command docs use ' — ' (em-dash).
Task 6 uses git add -A, contradicting CLAUDE.md safety rule to prefer adding specific files by name.
No explicit 'wait for approval before Step 4' gate in closing instruction, unlike the uniform gate language in Steps 2, 4, and 5.
No 'wait for approval' closing gate statement analogous to Steps 2, 4, and 5, making the stopping behaviour implicit rather than enforced.
Writing style block (em-dash policy) is duplicated verbatim in legal.md, log.md, and manifest.md — four copies that will drift independently.
Reference-mode description says 'prints snippet to chat if CLAUDE.md does not exist' but command now prompts to create CLAUDE.md first (commit 3d87e3d).
Stop condition 'No CLAUDE.md + Reference mode: snippet printed, nothing written' is now only one branch, not the only outcome — stale after commit 3d87e3d.
Intro says 'two confirmation gates' but the command has three: risk warning (Step 2), plan confirmation (Step 4), and force-push confirmation (Step 7).
Docs page omits the 'Document versions instead of containerizing' guidance block (mobile, desktop, browser-extension, library cases) present in the step file.
Top-level description field duplicates the identical string already inside plugins[0].description on line 12.
Commands table links to docs/commands/*.md with no indication that actual command logic lives in commands/*.md — the distinction is invisible at point of discovery.
git filter-repo called preferred over filter-branch but the command block uses filter-branch — no filter-repo invocation provided.
Step 5 uses git add -A, violating CLAUDE.md safety rule to prefer specific file names and risking accidental inclusion of .env files in a tagged release commit.
Step 5 Task 6 uses git add -A for the final archive commit, risking accidental inclusion of .env files or credentials in a sealed archive push.
Cross-reference to safety.md uses relative filesystem path (.claude/rules/safety.md) that assumes a specific installation location.
Code Quality section scoping language ('after all work for a prompt is complete') differs from docs version ('run before pushing, regardless of mode').
Approval gates section lists seven points but Step 5 Task 5 (Stop Services) contains an eighth gate not listed.
Deep Mode description says 'all five categories' but never names them; the command explicitly names them.
Step 7 says max 4 options but the command's selection list only names four categories omitting Performance; users will see Performance findings but cannot select it independently.
Docs page omits 'Demo accounts or demo data' and 'Recommended restoration approach' items that appear in the step file scan list.
Docs page omits the report output format section entirely (eight sections defined in the step file), unlike every other archive docs page.
Consolidation decision table is missing a | --- | separator row, making it syntactically inconsistent with all other tables in the project.
Step 5 description says 'stops if origin still points to company repo' but the command actually guides reconfiguration interactively rather than halting.
Claim that plugin.json is 'the only version file' is not enforced and will become stale if a secondary version reference is added elsewhere.
Step 1 is labeled Branch check but lacks '## Step 1 —' prefix and uses --- separators inconsistently with how other commands structure their steps.
Scan exclusion list hard-codes PHP/Laravel paths (vendor/, storage/) with no equivalent exclusions for Python, Ruby, or Go projects.
Auto-Commit cross-reference wording differs between the shipped rule and the doc page, creating ambiguity about whether it is advisory or prescriptive.
Lint instruction 'Skip silently if not configured — never push with lint errors' is logically contradictory: skip implies no enforcement, never push implies enforcement.
Docs version of the lint instruction repeats the same logical ambiguity as rules/git.md without resolving it.
Document specs table for privacy-policy omits the Cookies section that the command requires as section 8 when cookies are detected.
'Archive' action value present in step file consolidation table but omitted from the corresponding docs page.
docker save command uses bare {image_name} placeholder but the filename uses {service} — inconsistent, undefined variable.
Opening instruction runs 'ls -la' unconditionally on invocation with no opt-out; every other command presents a check or confirmation before any action.

Project Config Check is referenced twice (Full and Gap sections) with the skip condition only described within the block itself, creating a hidden conditional agents must track across non-adjacent sections.
Branch structure list (feature/*, fix/*, chore/*, refactor/*) is an incomplete subset of Conventional Commits types; agents enforcing it would reject docs/, test/, perf/, ci/, build/ branches.
Restoration strategy matrix (lines 43–59) is duplicated almost verbatim in the docs page; two near-identical tables will inevitably drift.
Output format section (nearly half the file) restates rules already covered in the Rules section, inflating token cost and risking agents treating duplicated content as additive constraints.
Hard Safety Rules section repeats constraints already stated in Behavior Rules, adding length without adding safety guarantees.
Step 3 scans last 20 commits for Conventional Commits detection then separately runs git log for version calculation — two reads when one would serve both.
Deep Mode has no defined maximum chunk size or agent cap; total agent cost is unbounded on large monorepos.
Scan Targets list includes Laravel Sail — a Laravel-specific tool irrelevant to the majority of non-PHP projects.
Environment Branches section embeds git branch -r command inline as prose, coupling the rule to a specific detection mechanism.
Document specs table duplicates structural information already fully specified in the command's per-document sections, creating a second drift surface.
Tasks list restates content already fully specified in the main body sections (Consolidation, Required Files, Optional File) with no new information.
Install section has no verification or smoke-test step to confirm commands appear in the picker after /reload-plugins, leaving silent cache failures undetected.
Step 4 silently skips if no test framework detected — ship will tag, push, and create a GitHub Release with zero test validation.
No checkpoint requiring docker load validation on exported tarballs; a corrupt export will not be detected until actual recovery years later.
No minimum coverage threshold for 'representative requests'; an agent may verify a single health-check endpoint and mark the entire collection as tested.
Known Trap for stale plugin cache has no automated verification or scripted workaround — relies entirely on developer memory each release.
No review gate between generating documents and committing — writes and immediately commits legal documents without asking the user to review.
No post-write verification after copying rule files — command reports written/updated/skipped with no actual content or existence check.
Minimum Evidence Checklist says 'infer from CI/hooks/pipelines' but no self-check instruction tells agents how to verify the risk inventory is complete or current.
No verification step to confirm the remote branch was actually deleted (e.g. git ls-remote --heads origin) before proceeding.
No self-check instruction confirming every env file pattern (.env, .env.staging, .env.production, .env.*.local) was searched before declaring credentials risk complete.
Post-rewrite verification only checks last 10 commits via git log --oneline -10; rewrite failures in older history go undetected.
No self-check instruction for agents to verify mode detection (Solo vs GitHub Flow) resolved correctly before proceeding.
Stop conditions section does not list 'written tests fail' even though the command says it stops and informs before committing if tests fail.
Task 8 says 'verify every active document is reachable from README.md' with no concrete link-tracing check; verification is aspirational rather than testable.
References filter-branch as primary tool and notes it is deprecated since Git 2.36, but provides no concrete filter-repo invocation as the stated preferred alternative.
Hard-codes GitLab as the private archive remote destination; developers using GitHub, Gitea, or Forgejo will be confused by the GitLab-specific prompts.
plugin.json carries a version field but marketplace.json has no version field, making the marketplace registration version-unaware.
--generate-notes flag will produce empty/unhelpful release notes for repos that commit directly to main without PRs — the exact audience of this plugin.
Docker base image pinning guidance uses mutable tags (node:18.17.1-alpine) instead of immutable digests (@sha256:...), undermining the long-term recovery guarantee.
Scan Targets list references Docker, Lando, Laravel Sail but omits current tooling (Dev Containers, Podman, Fly.io), giving agents false confidence in infrastructure coverage.
docker save | gzip uses a shell pipe that may silently fail or produce an empty file in non-Unix Docker environments (Windows, remote Docker context).
Does not specify Postman Collection format version (v2.0 vs v2.1) or whether Bruno/Insomnia formats are acceptable; v2.0 is not importable by Bruno without conversion.
Jekyll remote theme pinned to just-the-docs@v0.10.0; may not be the latest stable release and could miss security or compatibility patches.
Commit message template uses {version} placeholder that is never defined or read anywhere in legal.md.
Cloud/infrastructure scan target lists specific vendors (AWS, DO, Cloudflare) but omits GCP, Azure, Supabase, Vercel, Neon.
Governing law clause says 'laws of the jurisdiction in which the author resides' without naming the jurisdiction, making it unenforceable.
Terms of Service governing law clause has the same unnamed-jurisdiction problem as the EULA.

git-auto-commit: true silently skips the mandatory push confirmation (rules/safety.md lists push as always requiring confirmation); legal.md already carves out the correct exception, this file doesn't.
Same push-confirmation-bypass gap as adopt.md/manifest.md — git-auto-commit: true skips the mandatory push confirmation.
Same push-confirmation-bypass gap as adopt.md/log.md — git-auto-commit: true skips the mandatory push confirmation.
Step 7's auto-merge promotes real application code to environment branches with no CI-status gate at all, unlike ship.md's Steps 4/5 which explicitly check gh run list before promoting.
Solo Mode commits directly to main but never pushes it, unlike the GitHub Flow branch of the same step which explicitly pushes — commits silently diverge from origin in Solo Mode.
Same Solo-Mode-never-pushes gap as adopt.md/log.md/manifest.md.
Same Solo-Mode-never-pushes gap as adopt.md/legal.md/manifest.md.
Same Solo-Mode-never-pushes gap as adopt.md/legal.md/log.md.
Commit-scope-inference paragraph is duplicated verbatim across refactor.md and test.md instead of being centralized once in rules/git.md's Conventional Commits section and referenced by name.
Same scope-inference duplication as refactor.md — this is one of two copies in test.md.

Step 4's final blanket commit bundles secret cleanup, gitignore edits, sync fixes, and formatting into one multi-concern commit, and doesn't account for files the hardcoded-values sub-flow may have already committed per-file earlier in the same run.
Framework detection has no branch for a monorepo with multiple web packages/apps — which output location/format applies is undefined.
Branch-naming format refactor/{YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS} is an outlier — every other command uses {type}/{desc}-{YYYYMMDD} with no time component.

archive.md self-contradicts on whether Docker recovery tarballs are committed via Git LFS or gitignored — Step 2 summary and Stop-conditions describe an LFS-commit choice; the Output section and archive/2-restore-and-freeze.md both say the folder is unconditionally gitignored and never committed; archive/5-finalize.md (the actual Step 5 spec) has no user-facing commit-vs-local prompt at all.
States unconditionally that recovery/docker/ is gitignored and never committed, contradicting archive.md's Step 2/Step 5 prose describing an LFS-commit option.
Task 3 only auto-tracks files over 100MB via LFS with no user-facing commit-vs-keep-local prompt, contradicting archive.md's claim that Step 5 asks this as an explicit choice.

Stop-conditions list of 10 approval points omits archive/5-finalize.md's actual first gate (confirming the private archive remote URL before anything else) and includes a tarball commit-vs-local gate that doesn't exist in the child page as written.

Stop-conditions bullet "Step 1 complexity rated Blocked" is miscategorized — the very next clause says the user can approve and proceed, so it isn't a stop condition in the same sense as the rest of the list.
Missing a "Confirm completion" closing section describing the final report — log.md, manifest.md's declared twin, has one (### 6); manifest.md jumps straight from Step 5 to Stop conditions.
No final "Report" section describing what the closing report contains, despite the page's own mermaid diagram ending in Done([Report: tests added]) — every other multi-step command doc has one.

No "Before starting" section stating branch/git-strategy prerequisites, unlike every other command doc. Behavior is confirmed correct (env.md genuinely has no branch requirement) but the docs never say so explicitly, unlike normalize.md's precedent ("No branch requirement — runs from any branch").
Same missing "Before starting" section as env.md — test.md genuinely has no branch requirement, but the docs page never states this explicitly.
"(absence defaults to GitHub Flow, per git.md)" clarification present in adopt.md/legal.md's Before-starting section is missing here, though the underlying behavior is the same.
Same missing git-strategy-absence clarification as log.md.

Before-starting cleanup clause doesn't clarify how Gap Update's no-significant-changes outcome is treated for cleanup/commit purposes, unlike log.md's parallel clause which explicitly covers its analogous Outcome A case.

GitHub Flow branch-structure list is missing docs/*, test/*, perf/*, ci/*, build/* that are present in rules/git.md, and drops the "(or feat/*)" alias note next to feature/* — understates which branch types are actually sanctioned.

"Push still requires confirmation" is stated independently in both the Auto-Commit section and the Universal Rules → Safety subsection with no cross-reference tying the two together, risking one copy drifting from the other (this is the same underlying rule the c-001 command bugs violate).

The "Push still requires confirmation" bullet is displaced out of the Auto-Commit "When active" list — sits as an orphan bullet after the Exception paragraph instead of in its original list position, unlike rules/git.md's ordering.

Claims /helm:log, /helm:manifest, and /helm:adopt "do the same" (offer environment-branch promotion) after committing generated content — this specific claim isn't backed by anything in rules/git.md itself, which never asserts these commands actively promote.
One-line summary of git.md's contents omits the Auto-Commit and Deployment sections that exist in the actual file.

Asserts "Projects can extend the list, never shrink it" for the Agent Execution Boundaries list — this explicit prohibition doesn't exist anywhere in the actual rules/safety.md, which only says to document project-specific additions.

Drops "or similar" from the environment-branch name list (rules/git.md keeps it), presenting the six literal names as an exhaustive/closed list rather than the open-ended set the source rule describes.

Missing a "changes to this document" section that the other three legal docs (disclaimer, privacy-policy, terms) all share — eula.md's "Updates and Modifications" section addresses plugin/software version changes, not revisions to the EULA text itself.

Limitation-of-liability language is scoped differently across disclaimer.md, eula.md, and terms.md (different exclusion lists, only eula.md uses a dollar-cap) with no cross-reference reconciling the three.

Step 5 depends on knowing which branch the workflow was originally run from, but Step 1's report template never has a dedicated field requiring that to be stated explicitly — only implicit in branch-list prose.

Report output filenames (e.g. .archive/step1-explore.md) that later steps depend on by name are never specified by the producing step itself — likely handled by the orchestrator (archive.md), but the contract lives entirely outside the files responsible for it.
state.json is introduced with no prior setup/update/read instruction in steps 1-4 — unclear whether it's the same per-step resume cursor described elsewhere or a distinct end-of-archive marker.

Final commit unconditionally runs git add .gitattributes, which is only created under specific Task 3 branches (LFS commit, or "keep local" with other >100MB files) — fails with "pathspec did not match any files" if neither condition was met.

No guidance for resuming a step that was itself interrupted mid-execution (as opposed to a prior step being incomplete) — e.g. re-running after a partial Docker export re-does the whole export instead of detecting and reusing what already succeeded.

Depends on an implicit "is the app running" signal from Step 2's report prose, which has no dedicated field for it — inferred rather than stated; the fallback (mark requests unverified) makes this a minor gap, not a hard bug.
Command table lists only 9 of the 10 commands — /helm:adopt is missing from the table entirely, only mentioned later in prose.
The files array still lists "steps/", which no longer exists (renamed to prompts/ earlier this session) — packaging via this manifest would omit the step files /helm:archive actually needs.
Jekyll exclude list still has "steps/" instead of "prompts/" — the real prompts/archive/*.md step files aren't excluded, so they'll be pulled into the built site as pages instead of being skipped.

Known Traps' documented cache-copy command uses the glob ~/.claude/plugins/cache/helm@*/commands/, but the actual on-disk layout is ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-helm/helm/{version}/commands/ — confirmed the documented command literally fails with "no matches found".

Architecture Pointers claims _sass/ is part of the Jekyll site config alongside _config.yml and Gemfile, but no _sass/ directory exists — the site relies entirely on remote_theme with no local Sass overrides.
node_modules/ entry is dead weight — the repo has no package.json, npm, or any JS tooling anywhere; likely copied from a generic template.

just-the-docs gem is installed locally but the theme is activated via remote_theme in _config.yml, not the theme: key — the local gem dependency is likely never actually used, but removing it should be confirmed against how GitHub Pages resolves remote_theme before dropping it.

Step 5's category-selection AskUserQuestion hardcodes exactly 4 options (Architecture/Code Quality/Tests/Dependencies), permanently omitting Performance even though it has its own report section and completion-report line — Performance findings can never be selected for fixing.

Step 6 instructs setting user_status: skipped-by-user 'for files the user chose to skip in the confirmation step', but no per-file skip mechanism exists anywhere in the flow (Step 4 is all-or-nothing, Step 5 is tier-level) — this status has no writer.

No 'Before starting' git-strategy/branch check, unlike every other repo-mutating command — commits directly in Step 4 regardless of branch, which could commit straight to main under GitHub Flow, contradicting git.md's Universal Rule 'Never commit directly to main or master unless solo mode is active.'
Same missing 'Before starting' branch check as env.md — commits directly in Steps 4/5 with no git-strategy or branch check.

Step 4's commit staging handles a newly-created .env.example explicitly but has no equivalent for a newly-created .gitignore — if the Missing entries sub-flow creates a project's first .gitignore, git add -u won't stage it (only stages already-tracked files), so it's silently left out of the commit.

The three schema_version prose blocks (legal.md, refactor.md, test.md) aren't verbatim-consistent — legal.md adds a trailing 'Always write it going forward.' not present in refactor.md's block; minor wording drift, no functional bug.

Step 4 doc text says commits are gated by git.md's Auto-Commit rule with a confirmation prompt, but the real commands/env.md Step 4 has no AskUserQuestion and commits unconditionally every time — docs describe gated behavior that doesn't exist.

Step 5 doc text and mermaid flow omit the push-confirmation gate entirely — real commands/adopt.md Step 5 has an explicit 'Push main now?' AskUserQuestion before every push, in both Solo Mode and GitHub Flow, always required regardless of git-auto-commit.
Same missing push-confirmation gate as adopt.md/manifest.md's docs pages.
Same missing push-confirmation gate as adopt.md/log.md's docs pages.

'Framework and output detection' section and mermaid flow omit the monorepo-detection step entirely — real commands/legal.md Step 1 asks which package should receive the legal docs when multiple web packages are found, scoping the rest of the scan to that package.

'Existing documents' section never mentions the schema_version field the real command reads/writes in .claude/legal-manifest.json, including the 'treat a missing schema_version as 1' migration behavior.

Step 7 doc text and mermaid flow omit the CI-gate check before environment promotion — real commands/refactor.md Step 7 checks CI status for the pushed commit (gh run list, matched by SHA) and folds the result into the promotion confirmation.

Missing the 'Data Persistence' section entirely — the real prompts/archive/step2-restore-and-freeze.md explains that docker save captures the image but not the data volume, and describes the two recovery mechanisms; the parent archive.md overview mentions it briefly but this detail page omits it completely.
Missing the Postman Collection Format v2.1 schema detail and Bruno-compatibility rationale that the real prompts/archive/step3-postman.md specifies.

Claims /helm:ship treats 'fix' as the only non-feat/breaking type triggering a patch bump and 'anything else is ignored for versioning', but commands/ship.md explicitly gives perf the same patch-bump treatment as fix. Verified against actual ship.md content.

Link to /helm:adopt uses an absolute path (/docs/commands/adopt) missing both the .html extension and the site's /claude-helm baseurl prefix — the only absolute-path link in docs/, will 404 in production even though html-proofer's local check didn't flag it. Verified: sibling links in the same file correctly use relative rules/git.html-style paths.
Says 'Projects can extend the list, never shrink it', omitting the 'Document any project-specific additions' clause present in the real rules/safety.md.

Reads Step 1's 'Archiving from:' field with no defined fallback if an older Step1 report (created before this field was added) lacks it — contrast with step3-postman.md, which explicitly handles the analogous case for Step 2's 'App running' field.
'Rules:', 'Determine:', 'Guidance:' are plain bolded-colon labels, not '## ' headings, unlike the other four archive step files which all use '##' for the same structural role.

The output-format template embeds prompt-authoring rationale inline with the literal field value the executing model should produce (e.g. 'Archiving from: {current branch name} — Step 5's branch cleanup reads this field directly...') — risk the executing model echoes the explanatory aside verbatim into the generated report. Also affects step2-restore-and-freeze.md's App running field.

Organizes work as top-level '## Task N' headings interleaved with approval gates, while step2/step3/step4 each use a single '## Tasks' checklist separate from narrative — plausibly justified by Step 5's per-task approval gates, but worth a consistency pass.

plugins: whitelist lists jekyll-seo-tag and jekyll-remote-theme but not jekyll-include-cache (added to Gemfile this session). Verified local `bundle exec jekyll build` works fine without it (non-safe-mode Jekyll auto-requires all installed plugin gems), but GitHub Pages' hosted build runs in safe mode where the plugins: list does matter, and that path has never been tested (no CI) — adding it defensively removes the doubt.

Dev Commands says 'the Jekyll site is not built or verified locally as part of this repo's own workflow', but Gemfile now has a test group with html-proofer specifically for that; stale relative to this session's change, and doesn't document how to run it.

Known Traps says 'the Jekyll site build itself is never actually verified before or after a release', which overstates the current state now that html-proofer exists as a local verification step (still true it isn't wired into /helm:ship or CI).

Gemfile.lock is gitignored even though the project just added html-proofer as a test framework meant to verify the Jekyll build — without a committed lockfile, gem resolution (and therefore build/test results) isn't reproducible across machines or sessions.
The files array for the helm plugin package omits LICENSE — since plugin.json declares "license": "MIT", the distributed plugin package ships without the actual license text.
